references.text: Isaiah warns against seeking glory from people instead of from God, a theme that mirrors Jesus' criticism of the religious leaders in John 5:44.
Here it is emphasized that God created His people for His own glory, which contrasts with those who seek only human recognition.
God declares that He will not give His glory to others, which is central to Jesus' argument that they do not seek glory from the only God.
Jesus' warning against seeking glory from one another, but rather from the only God, is directly repeated in this verse.
Here those who love human glory more than God's glory are described, a direct parallel to the situation in John 5:44.
Paul describes the true Jew as receiving praise from God, not from people, which corresponds with the requirement to seek God's glory.
Paul speaks of having a good conscience and not seeking glory from people but from God, as a counterpoint to those criticized in John 5:44.
